summary: Resume-feature review for EIBIL (iteration 4). Extended /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py from 70 -> 85 tests covering: resume lifecycle (empty/upload/download/replace/delete, PDF+DOC+DOCX only, 5MB limit, oversize/wrong-type rejection), apply-with-resume (multipart answers+file), apply-without-file reuses profile resumeId, employer applicants row has email/phone/city + populated resumeId, employer resume download access rules (owner / applicant / report-viewer / 403 for others), verify-candidate snapshot.identity has email/phone/city/resumeAvailable + resumeId on response, GET /employer/reports/:id resumeId check. All 84/85 PASS; 1 confirmed backend bug remains: GET /api/v1/employer/reports/:id does NOT include resumeId in its response (verify-candidate POST does, so re-opening a report from the Reports table loses the resume download button). Frontend audit: employee /employee/account is MISSING the entire 'My resume' panel (no ResumeManager, no resume-panel/resume-upload-btn/resume-current/resume-download/resume-delete test ids anywhere in /app/frontend/src/pages/employee/Account.jsx). All other required frontend test ids (resume-upload-input, resume-upload-clear, easy-apply-button, applicants-table, applicant-contact-<id>, applicant-resume-<id>, applicant-report-<id>, report-contact, report-download-resume, report-no-resume) are present and wired to the services.

critical.issue: Response omits resumeId. reportService.getForEmployer returns the VerificationCheck doc as-is; it should also include profile.resumeId (same shape as generateForEmployer at line 87). As a result, re-opening a historical report from the Reports table shows no 'Download resume' button even if the candidate has a resume. Fix: in reportService.getForEmployer, after loading the check, do `const profile = await EmployeeProfile.findById(check.employeeId).select('resumeId').lean()` and return `{ ...check, resumeId: profile?.resumeId || null }`.

minor.issue: fileFilter accepts application/octet-stream unconditionally. resumeService.assertFile does a filename-regex fallback, but if a client sends octet-stream with a non-pdf/doc/docx filename extension spelled oddly (e.g., 'resume.PDF.exe'), assertFile's /\.(pdf|doc|docx)$/i still passes because the extension check is case-insensitive and anchored at end — benign today but worth tightening to a strict allow-list on both mimetype and basename extension.

When applying WITH a file, setCurrent() replaces the candidate's profile resume and DELETES the previous Resume doc — but prior Application records still carry the old resumeId and their .populate('resumeId','fileName') now returns null (observed in test: Priya's Acme pipeline row has null resumeId after a later re-upload). Consider either copying the Resume per-application or NOT auto-deleting the old resume if any Application still references it.

ui_bugs.issue: The 'My resume' panel is NOT implemented anywhere under /employee/account. None of the required test ids resume-panel, resume-empty, resume-upload-btn, resume-upload-input (on account page), resume-current, resume-download, resume-delete exist in the frontend. Backend endpoints and employeeService.uploadResume/downloadResume are wired, but no UI calls them from the account page. Candidates cannot replace or delete their resume from the account; they can only upload via the apply flow.

integration_issues.flow: Employer re-opens a historical report (Reports table -> Open)
integration_issues.issue: ReportView.resumeId is undefined because the GET endpoint does not return resumeId; UI falls through to data-testid='report-no-resume' even when a resume exists.

action_items: FIX reportService.getForEmployer to include resumeId (match generateForEmployer).

IMPLEMENT the My-Resume panel on /employee/account with the required test ids (resume-panel, resume-empty, resume-upload-btn, resume-upload-input, resume-current, resume-download, resume-delete). Wire it to employeeService.uploadResume/downloadResume/deleteResume/getResume (already defined).
Consider decoupling Application.resumeId lifetime from profile re-uploads so historical applicant rows don't lose their resume.
critical_code_review_comments: resumeService.setCurrent uses EmployeeProfile.findOneAndUpdate without {new:false}; it relies on the default pre-update doc to grab the old resumeId for deletion. OK today but will break if someone adds {new:true}. Add an explicit comment or {returnDocument:'before'}.

resumeService.employerCanRead checks VerificationCheck.exists({employerId, employeeId: profile._id}) but does NOT limit by recency (employer who viewed once has permanent access). Consider a TTL (e.g., last 90 days) or revocation hook when the candidate deletes their resume.
resumeService.read returns the full Buffer from Mongo for every download; for large/concurrent traffic this will balloon memory. Consider streaming or object storage.
employerController.downloadResume performs the access check and the read sequentially via two require() calls; works but readability suffers — hoist resumeService to top of file.
uploadMiddleware.resume treats 'application/octet-stream' as allowed to accept quirky browsers; combine with resumeService.assertFile's extension regex to form a single allow-list.
reportService.getForEmployer: beyond missing resumeId, consider populating viewerUserId/employeeId like list endpoints so the ReportView does not need extra calls.

rca of the issue: reportService.generateForEmployer (POST /verify-candidate) correctly returns `{ ...check.toObject(), resumeId: profile.resumeId || null }` (line 87), so the UI shows report-download-resume on the fresh snapshot. But getForEmployer (GET /employer/reports/:id, used by the Reports table 'Open' action) returns just the lean VerificationCheck without re-attaching resumeId, so the client receives `report.resumeId === undefined` and renders data-testid='report-no-resume'. Reproduction: hr@acmetech.in -> verify Priya by EIBIL ID (download button visible) -> navigate away -> open same row from /employer/reports -> button disappears. Mitigation (one line): in getForEmployer, after `if (!check) throw…`, add `const prof = await EmployeeProfile.findById(check.employeeId).select('resumeId').lean(); return { ...check, resumeId: prof?.resumeId || null };`.
